summary:
The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 (Public Law 118-31, enacted December 22, 2023) authorizes appropriations and sets policy for the Department of Defense, national security programs of the Department of Energy, and related agencies for fiscal year 2024. The Act is organized into seven divisions covering defense authorizations, military construction, energy national security, funding tables, other matters, State Department authorization, and intelligence authorization.

**Procurement and research.** The Act authorizes procurement and research, development, test, and evaluation (RDT&E) funding through detailed line-item tables. Army procurement is authorized at $3,313,210 thousand for aircraft, $4,945,267 thousand for missiles, $4,704,617 thousand for weapons and tracked vehicles, and $8,725,753 thousand for other procurement. Navy aircraft procurement is authorized at $18,008,909 thousand. Army RDT&E totals $15,966,152 thousand and Navy RDT&E $26,722,557 thousand. The Act permits multiyear procurement of up to 13 Virginia-class (Block VI) submarines and up to six Auxiliary Personnel Lighter vessels, with termination-liability limits, and directs upgrades to at least 24 V-22 aircraft.

**Force structure limits.** The Air Force may not retire more than 68 F-15E aircraft through September 30, 2029, may not retire RQ-4 aircraft or reduce inventory below 10 through September 30, 2028, and may temporarily reduce fighter inventory to no fewer than 1,112 aircraft until October 1, 2024. Case-by-case exceptions apply for non-mission-capable aircraft.

**Personnel policy and compensation.** The Act makes permanent the authority to recall retired members to active duty; prohibits requiring or barring gender/pronoun identification in official correspondence; and restricts certain post-service employment with foreign governments of concern, subject to waivers. It expands continuation-pay eligibility (from 7 to 12 years of service), extends numerous expiring pay authorities to December 31, 2024, and authorizes monthly bonus pay for junior members through 2024. Members involuntarily separated solely for refusing the COVID-19 vaccine may request reinstatement consideration within two years.

**Organization and oversight.** Provisions establish a Strategic Cybersecurity Program and an Electromagnetic Warfare chapter (new 10 U.S.C. ch. 25), extend the "Never Contract with the Enemy" authority (renamed and sunset extended to December 31, 2033), and require assessments of training ranges, Marine Corps Force Design 2030, and audit-readiness metrics.

**Foreign relations.** The Act creates Indo-Pacific campaigning and maritime domain awareness initiatives, requires biannual U.S.-Israel military exercises, strengthens Taiwan defense cooperation and oversight, caps clandestine operational-preparation spending at $40 million per fiscal year, and reaffirms the one-China policy.

**Military construction and other funds.** Division B authorizes defense agency construction, with notable amounts including Fort Meade, Maryland ($885,000,000) and Guantanamo Bay, Cuba ($257 million). The Act authorizes transfer of $172,000,000 for the Lovell Federal Health Care Center and $77,000,000 for the Armed Forces Retirement Home. It authorizes $198,500,000 for the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy and $500,000,000 for the Maritime Administration's port infrastructure development program.

**State Department (Division F).** Provisions address Foreign Service personnel, chief-of-mission staffing, anti-retaliation and workforce surveys, internships at international organizations ($1,500,000 authorized), and reports on countering PRC infrastructure investment.

**Intelligence (Division G).** The Act reforms CIA handling of sexual assault and harassment, creating confidential reporting, a privileged victim-advocate relationship, and a Special Victim Investigator required to complete investigations within 60 days. It also addresses commercial remote sensing requirements, AI/machine-learning guidance for intelligence products, and expanded assessment of PRC economic and technological capabilities.

**Miscellaneous.** Division E includes the Preventing Child Sex Abuse Act of 2023 (amending 18 U.S.C. 2423 to lower the intent standard and add penalties up to 30 years), a federal charter for the National American Indian Veterans, Inc., and immigration and overtime-pay provisions. Numerous reports, briefings, and deadlines are specified throughout, many due in 2024.
